raw_content: {"cards":[{"title":"Two-Format Creative System: Top-of-Funnel Problem/Solution and Bottom-of-Funnel Objection Ads","summary":"Build only extreme top-of-funnel problem-solution ads and extreme bottom-of-funnel objection ads, letting middle-funnel coverage happen naturally.","use_when":"Deciding what creative concepts to brief for a paid social campaign, so you stop wasting production budget on vague middle-funnel ads.","steps":["Split all creative into two formats: top-of-funnel problem/solution ads and bottom-of-funnel objection-handling ads.","For top-of-funnel, address the core problem the avatar has and position your product as the unique solution. Problems can be functional (back pain) or identity/emotional (clothing makes you feel cool, part of something).","For bottom-of-funnel, make one ad per objection (price vs. competitor, warranty/expiration, delivery speed, quality doubt). Show one specific proof point per ad rather than dumping all benefits.","Accept that longer, hook-heavy top-of-funnel ads will naturally bleed into the middle of the funnel; shorter or simpler versions of either format cover the middle-bottom gap.","Do not build dedicated middle-funnel creative unless you have a specific reason.","Run catalog/DPA retargeting to anyone who viewed similar products as the non-creative bottom-of-funnel layer."],"caveats":["The source presents this as the currently working approach in the 'Andromeda era'; funnel economics shift as platform algorithms change.","Skipping middle-funnel creative is a deliberate trade-off relying on natural spillover; some categories with long consideration cycles may need explicit middle creative."],"tags":["paid-social-creative","funnel-strategy","creative-strategy","objection-handling","top-of-funnel","bottom-of-funnel","meta-ads"]},{"title":"Creative Hit Rate: Measure Winning Ads Instead of Total Ads Launched","summary":"Define a creative hit rate as winning ads divided by total ads launched, and scale creative volume only when hit rate quality is maintained.","use_when":"Evaluating whether to increase ad production volume, or auditing why a high-volume creative testing program is underperforming.","steps":["Define a 'high-performing ad' upfront using two criteria: it spent more than 5% of total campaign budget AND hit your target CPA.","Calculate hit rate = (number of high-performing ads) / (total ads launched) × 100.","Interpret it: launching 100 ads with 5 winning ads is a 5% hit rate, described by the source as a solid, fairly normal benchmark. Volume negates luck, so 1,000 ads at the same hit rate implies ~50 winners.","Before producing more ads, ask whether each new ad has a genuine chance to be a winner. Only scale volume if the baseline quality holds.","When volume rises but hit rate falls, treat that as a signal you are diluting quality, not scaling."],"caveats":["The 5%-spend threshold and 5% hit rate are the source's own definitions and heuristics, not industry standards.","Increasing volume only compounds if hit rate is stable; otherwise you multiply low-quality spend."],"tags":["paid-social-creative","measurement","creative-strategy","testing","meta-ads","roas"]},{"title":"Avoid Flooding the Pixel With Low-Quality Creative That Creates Negative Events","summary":"Understand that Meta's pixel and delivery train on all traffic including non-converters, so unqualified clicks actively degrade targeting.","use_when":"Deciding whether to bulk-upload thousands of AI/UGC ads, or diagnosing declining account performance despite rising spend.","steps":["Recognize the mechanism: the pixel fires, sends signal events to Meta, and delivery optimizes based on the purchase event to find similar buyers at lower CPA.","Understand that the pixel also trains on negative events — bounces, carts not converted, unqualified traffic — not just purchases.","Realize that flooding an account with thousands of low-quality ads disperses budget and generates negative events that mis-train the pixel and degrade targeting accuracy.","Before scaling creative count, vet each ad for its likelihood of attracting the right avatar; reject ads likely to pull unqualified clicks even if they are cheap to produce.","Treat the pixel's recent event stream as a quality signal to protect, not just a volume number to grow."],"caveats":["This is the source's explanation of Meta pixel training, not a documented platform spec; algorithm behavior changes and should be re-verified in the current interface.","The source does not provide a quantified threshold for how many negative events cause harm."],"tags":["paid-social-creative","algorithm-mechanics","meta-ads","pixel","conversion-optimization","measurement"]},{"title":"Avatar-and-Angle Framework for Top-of-Funnel Concepts","summary":"Turn one avatar's full list of problems into ad angles, then pair each angle with the avatar to form a top-of-funnel concept.","use_when":"Generating top-of-funnel ad concepts and creative briefs for a product, especially when stuck for angles.","steps":["Define one avatar (your ICP) at a time — the specific person you are selling to.","List every problem that avatar has, including problems not obviously related to your product; each problem becomes a potential ad angle.","Combine one avatar with one angle to create a concept/packaged ad.","Write ads that explicitly call out the avatar and their problem, then position your product as the solution.","Note the source's claim that the algorithm tends to show ads mentioning a specific group to that group (e.g., an 'if you're ex-X' ad reaching ex-X people), reinforcing the need for explicit avatar callouts.","Repeat across multiple avatars who can buy the same product for different purposes — e.g., a greens product framed for GLP-1 weight-loss users vs. for hair growth."],"caveats":["The algorithm-matches-avatar behavior is the source's claim about the Andromeda era and may not hold universally or persist.","Listing unrelated problems can dilute relevance; the source frames it as a brainstorming step, then you select the strongest angles."],"tags":["paid-social-creative","customer-research","creative-strategy","positioning","avatar-framework","top-of-funnel","meta-ads"]},{"title":"Mine Bottom-of-Funnel Objections by Calling Checkout Abandoners","summary":"Discover real purchase objections by phoning customers who abandoned checkout and by writing down objections you already know, then build one objection ad each.","use_when":"Building bottom-of-funnel retargeting creative or diagnosing why add-to-cart does not convert to purchase.","steps":["First, write down every objection to buying your product that you already know (price, shipping, trust, warranty).","Second, call customers who literally abandoned their checkout and ask why they did not purchase. The source calls this the best method for surfacing true bottom-of-funnel objections.","Convert each surfaced objection into its own ad: price objection → value/quality proof or competitor comparison; warranty objection → show the guarantee; delivery objection → show speed.","Keep each bottom-of-funnel ad focused on one objection and one proof point, not a full feature list.","Example from source: a hair product ad stating a single clinical claim, and a cookware ad leveraging a lifetime warranty to counter competitors' limited warranties."],"caveats":["Abandoned-checkout calls require customer contact data and may have low response rates; the source presents it as high-signal but does not quantify outcomes.","Results of example ads are illustrative, not guaranteed benchmarks."],"tags":["paid-social-creative","objection-handling","customer-research","bottom-of-funnel","retargeting","creative-strategy"]},{"title":"Structure the Ad Account as Avatar/Angle 'Packs' Inside One CBO Campaign","summary":"Use a single CBO prospecting campaign with many ad sets ('packs'), each grouping ads by a single avatar and angle or funnel position.","use_when":"Setting up or restructuring a Meta ad account so you can read results and control spend by avatar, angle and funnel stage.","steps":["Create one core prospecting campaign (e.g., 'ML Prospecting') using auction buying and a Sales objective.","Set daily budget to where you are currently comfortable — the source warns not to use budget as a lever to increase spend, and suggests a rough floor of at least 1× your target CPA.","Choose bidding (highest volume or value) and keep budget scheduling at 'none'.","Set audience segment reporting: engaged segments = site visitors last 30 days and add-to-cart last 90 days; existing customers = 180-day purchasers (not all-time).","Name each ad set as a 'pack' with a sequence number plus avatar and angle, and label the funnel position (top or bottom).","Exclude existing customers from the prospecting campaign; leave placements wide open; select the correct dataset and the purchase conversion event.","Use a standard attribution setting (source uses 7-day click, 1-day engaged-view, 1-day view). Do not use dynamic creative or live video ads.","Launch each new batch of ads into a new pack. You can run dozens of packs in one campaign — the source reports accounts with 30–100 ad sets — which allows control via value rules, minimums and maximums instead of pausing ads.","Expect the pattern over time: top-of-funnel packs spend more and scale further at lower ROAS; bottom-of-funnel packs convert better but scale less."],"caveats":["Menu names (buying type, performance goal, attribution windows) change as Meta updates the interface — verify current settings.","Performance goal choice: maximize conversions for single-product or equal-price brands, value of conversions when prices vary.","The 1× target CPA daily budget is a rough starting heuristic, not a rule.","Packs beyond the core prospecting campaign (retargeting, retention, scale campaign) exist but the source does not detail them here."],"tags":["paid-social-creative","campaign-setup","meta-ads","account-structure","cbo","ad-sets","measurement"]}]

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a specific Meta ad account structure designed to optimize pixel training and creative hit rates by separating campaigns strictly into top-of-funnel (problem/solution) and bottom-of-funnel (objection handling) ad sets. modules: [ADC] topics: [campaign setup and tracking, algorithm mechanics] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. campaign setup and tracking / Establishing an ad account structure that isolates top-of-funnel and bottom-of-funnel creatives into separate ad sets (referred to as "packs") within a single Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) environment. Naming conventions and setup for top-of-funnel packs, focusing exclusively on pairing an ideal customer avatar with a specific problem-solution angle (e.g., "Weight loss GLP-1 supplement"). Configuring bottom-of-funnel packs to focus solely on overcoming objections (e.g., price, warranty, delivery speed) identified through post-purchase surveys and abandoned checkout calls. algorithm mechanics / Explaining how the Meta pixel trains its delivery algorithms based on the quality of traffic it receives. Warning against the strategy of flooding an ad account with thousands of low-quality creatives, as driving unqualified traffic generates "negative events" (e.g., high bounce rates or abandoned carts) that actively mis-train the pixel and degrade overall account performance. Introducing the "Creative Hit Rate" formula (number of high-performing ads divided by the total number of ads launched) to emphasize that increasing creative volume only scales an account if the baseline quality of the ads is maintained.

Look for. The primary reason flooding an ad account with high volumes of low-quality creative hurts performance: the Meta pixel trains on all traffic, so driving unqualified clicks generates "negative events" that actively mis-train the algorithm and degrade targeting accuracy. The definition of "Creative Hit Rate": the percentage of ads that spend more than 5% of the total campaign budget and successfully hit the target CPA, calculated by dividing the number of high-performing ads by the total number launched. The recommended ad account structure for top and bottom of funnel: grouping ads by avatar and angle into distinct ad sets ("packs") within a single CBO campaign, rather than mixing awareness levels. The best method for discovering bottom-of-funnel objections to address in ads: calling customers who abandoned their checkout to ask why they didn't purchase.
